title: Closures
summary: A function that remembers the local variables from where it was created. Callbacks, private state, and per-player data all rely on closures.

details.heading: Upvalues
details.body: A local referenced by an inner function becomes an *upvalue*: it lives on even after the outer function returns, shared by every closure that captured it.

details.heading: Sharing vs copying
details.body: Multiple closures created in the same scope share the same upvalue. Closures created in different loop iterations capture different variables in Luau (per-iteration loop vars).

explanation.whatItIs: When a function is created, it takes an invisible snapshot of the local variables around it — and carries that snapshot wherever it goes. That function+snapshot pair is a closure.
explanation.whyItExists: Roblox is callback-driven: you hand functions to events and timers that fire later. Closures let those callbacks still see your variables when they finally run.
whenToUse: Event callbacks that need your local data: `part.Touched:Connect(function(hit) ... use myLocal ... end)`
Private state: a counter variable only the returned function can touch
Factory functions that produce customized functions
whenNotToUse: Don't capture large tables you don't need — captured locals stay alive as long as the closure does (memory)
Don't rely on closures where a simple parameter would be clearer
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
local function makeCounter()
    local count = 0                  -- captured!
    return function()
        count += 1                   -- still alive in here
        return count
    end
end

local tick = makeCounter()
print(tick())  --> 1
print(tick())  --> 2    -- count persists between calls
```
The inner function packed `count` in its suitcase when it left home.
tips: Closures are how debounce/cooldown patterns remember their last-use time
Every `Connect(function() ... end)` inside a function captures that function's locals — usually exactly what you want
Use closures for encapsulation instead of script-level globals
commonMistakes: Assuming captured variables were copied at creation time — they're live references; later changes are visible
Creating closures in loops expecting independent copies of a shared local (Luau loop vars are per-iteration, but your own locals declared outside the loop are shared)
Forgetting closures keep upvalues alive — a closure stored forever keeps its captured data forever

examples.title: A private counter (no globals)
examples.code:
local function makeCounter(start)
    local count = start or 0
    return {
        add = function(n) count += (n or 1) end,
        get = function() return count end,
    }
end

local score = makeCounter(100)
score.add(25)
print(score.get())   --> 125
-- `count` itself is unreachable from outside — private!

examples.title: Callbacks capturing locals
examples.code:
local function setupButton(button, reward)
    local claimed = false    -- captured by the closure below
    button.Activated:Connect(function(player)
        if claimed then return end
        claimed = true
        print(player.Name .. " claimed " .. reward)
    end)
end

setupButton(script.Parent, "100 coins")
examples.whyItWorks: The connected callback runs much later, but still sees `claimed` and `reward` — they were captured when the closure was made.
